capabilities.target: user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt and treated as the user's own instructions

instructions.note: The agent is told to save anything useful about preferences or standing instructions with no filter on the trustworthiness of the source, so content from untrusted web research can be persisted.

Recalled memories are explicitly granted the authority of the user's own direct instructions, with no provenance check, so anything that reached memory -- including content copied from untrusted web pages -- commands the agent in future sessions as if the user said it.

controls.name: Memory provenance tagging and source-trust filtering on writes
controls.decay_rationale: Effective only if provenance is attached and checked by the memory store itself rather than left to the model to self-report; the artifacts show no such enforcement today.

controls.name: Keep recalled memory in an untrusted data channel, never merge it into the instruction channel
controls.decay_rationale: Must be enforced by the harness (separate message role, no execution authority) rather than by a prompt instruction telling the model to 'treat it as untrusted'; the latter would only be partially_dependent at best.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action review) before any email send
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action review gate does not decay with model capability, though it depends on approval volume and reviewer attentiveness (approval fatigue); none exists today per runtime notes.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to a vetted contacts record
controls.decay_rationale: The destination comes from a system of record rather than from model output, so it does not decay with capability and makes attacker-controlled addresses unreachable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Scope drive.read credential to least privilege, excluding confidential folders by default
controls.decay_rationale: A narrower credential scope does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Audit log of memory writes and email sends with reviewer alerting
controls.decay_rationale: Detective only; reduces consequence if reviewed before harm completes but does not change tier credit.

findings.title: Untrusted web content poisons persistent agent memory with no provenance or review (ASI06)

attack_path.note: Untrusted web page content encountered during research
Agent is instructed to save anything useful about preferences or standing instructions, with no source-trust filtering or provenance tagging

forecast.watch_signal: No controls currently constrain this path, so the tier is already at the ceiling; watch for any new write-capable tool or expanded memory scope, which would only broaden the poisoning surface.

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to save anything useful about preferences or standing instructions via memory.save, with no restriction based on the source of that information.

memory.save accepts free text and there is no provenance on memory entries, and the user never reviews them, so content originating from untrusted web pages fetched during research can be persisted as if it were a standing instruction.

recommendations.action: Attach provenance to every memory write and reject or quarantine writes sourced from untrusted web content pending review (ctrl.memory_provenance).
Stop merging recalled memory into the instruction channel at recall time; treat it as untrusted context (ctrl.memory_trust_separation).
Log every memory write with its source and surface anomalous writes for review (ctrl.audit_logging).

findings.title: Memory laundering feeds a lethal trifecta: poisoned 'instructions' drive confidential drive reads into unrestricted email send (TC5 + TC1, ASI01/ASI02)

attack_path.note: Memories recalled at session start, including any poisoned entries, are injected into the system prompt and treated as the user's own instructions (prompt.md:4)
The poisoned 'instruction' directs the agent to read the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files
The poisoned 'instruction' directs the agent to send the retrieved confidential content to an address of the attacker's choosing, with no approval gate

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No preventive, approval, or scoping control exists on this path today, so the tier is already at the ceiling; watch for drive scope being broadened or for any future approval gate being added and later removed.

evidence.observation: Recalled memories are explicitly treated as the user's own instructions, with no distinction by source trust.

memory.save accepts free text with no provenance, and recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session, so any poisoned entry is re-asserted as a standing instruction every session.

mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the full drive including confidential work files, so a poisoned instruction can direct confidential data to an attacker-chosen address with no human check; binding the recipient to a vetted contacts record would make attacker-controlled destinations unreachable regardless of model behavior.

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw action review (not a model summary) before any email send (ctrl.email_approval_gate).
Bind the send recipient to a vetted contacts record rather than a model-chosen address (ctrl.email_recipient_allowlist); this severs the path to attacker-controlled destinations.
Scope drive.read to least privilege, excluding confidential folders by default (ctrl.drive_scope_limit).
Stop treating recalled memory as trusted instruction (ctrl.memory_trust_separation); this is the root cause that lets the poisoned entry drive these actions.
Log drive reads and email sends with recipient and content summary for post-hoc review (ctrl.audit_logging).

rating.rationale: The design has no provenance, filtering, approval, or scoping controls on any of its three capabilities. Untrusted web content encountered during research can be written into long-term memory with no review (ASI06), and the system prompt explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memory as the user's own direct instruction with no distinction by source (prompt.md:4). That single design choice converts a storage write (S2) into a durable, self-reinforcing command channel that can direct the agent's most severe capability -- unrestricted, unapproved, irreversible email send of confidential drive content (S3) -- producing a textbook memory-laundering-into-lethal-trifecta chain (TC5 + TC1). Because zero controls are declared on this path, residual equals inherent at critical for both findings, and the forecast also stays at critical: there is nothing left to decay. The priority is not monitoring for future trigger events but adding baseline structural controls now -- provenance-tagged memory, separation of recalled memory from the instruction channel, a raw-action approval gate on email send, and a recipient allowlist bound to a vetted contacts record, which would sever the egress path to attacker-controlled destinations.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or runtime policy configuration was provided; exact credential scopes and data sensitivity of individual memory entries are inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes.
No information was given on session frequency, volume of memory entries, or typical recipient domains, which limits precision beyond the qualitative likelihood and consequence bands used here.

Autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) were not declared and are conservatively treated as unbounded, which triggers the rubric's autonomy modifier on S2/S3 sinks; if the deployment in fact enforces step or runtime limits, this should be supplied and the assessment rerun.
